meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for time.

examples.text: いつまでも待っています。

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Connects a contrasting fact or trails off at the end of a sentence to voice a polite objection.

examples.text: お風呂に入りましたけど。
examples.trans: I already took a bath, though.

examples.text: 高いけど、おいしいです。

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Casual sentence-ending particle.

examples.trans: Well, that's just how it is.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
Adverb emphasizing that there is nothing more.

examples.text: ただ本当のことを言っただけです。
ただ静かに待っていた。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Auxiliary na-adjective expressing resemblance or conjecture.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 彼は忙しいみたいですね。

やれる.gloss: can do; be able to manage

meanings.en: can do; be able to pull off
meanings.note: Potential ichidan form of やる (to do).

examples.text: 自分にやれることをやるだけだ。
examples.trans: I just do what I can do.

examples.text: 君ならきっとやれるよ。
examples.trans: You can definitely pull it off.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Loanword from English 'sales'.

examples.text: これからセールスに行きます。
examples.trans: I'm going out on sales calls now.

examples.text: セールスの仕事は大変です。

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'part'.

examples.text: ここからが一番面白いパートだ。
examples.trans: From here on is the most interesting part.

examples.text: 次のパートに進みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's move on to the next part.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (一番近い), forms the superlative ('closest').

examples.trans: This one is the most popular.

examples.text: 一番近い駅はどこですか。

meanings.note: A short excerpt from a book, speech, or song.

examples.text: 有名な小説の一節を引用した。
examples.trans: He quoted a passage from a famous novel.

examples.text: その詩の一節が心に残っている。
examples.trans: A verse from that poem stays in my heart.

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Formal noun; pairs with する.

examples.text: 先生の助言に感謝しています。
examples.trans: I am grateful for my teacher's advice.

examples.text: 少し助言をいただけますか。
examples.trans: Could you give me some advice?

meanings.en: turn toward; face; be suited for
meanings.note: Godan verb; in 気が向く, means 'to feel like doing'.

examples.text: 気が向いたら連絡してください。
examples.trans: Please contact me whenever you feel like it.

examples.text: こっちを向いてください。

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb (える).

examples.text: 新しい知識を得ることができた。
examples.trans: I was able to gain new knowledge.

examples.text: 多くの人の信頼を得た。
examples.trans: He earned the trust of many people.

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.trans: Are you in your right mind?

meanings.en: be decided; be settled; be certain
meanings.note: Intransitive godan verb; ～に決まっている means 'it is certain/obvious that...'.

examples.text: 明日の予定が決まりました。
彼が勝つに決まっている。

meanings.note: Literary noun; 真の + noun means 'true/genuine'.

examples.text: 真の自由を求めて旅に出た。
examples.trans: He set out on a journey seeking true freedom.

meanings.en: know; find out; be aware of
meanings.note: Godan verb; state of knowing is 知っている.

examples.text: 彼の電話番号を知っていますか。
examples.trans: Do you know his phone number?

examples.text: 本当の理由を知りたい。
examples.trans: I want to know the real reason.

meanings.note: Acknowledges that what the other person pointed out really is true.

examples.text: 確かにそのとおりですね。
確かに受け取りました。

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 今日は空がとても青いですね。
examples.trans: The sky is very blue today, isn't it?
Birds are flying in the sky.

meanings.en: return to; go back to (one's roots/basics)
meanings.note: Compound godan verb.

examples.text: 原点に立ち返って考えよう。
examples.trans: Let's go back to the basics and think.

examples.text: 初心に立ち返ることが大切だ。
examples.trans: It's important to return to one's original intention.

meanings.note: Reflexive pronoun pointing back to the person under discussion.

examples.text: 自分の言葉で話します。
examples.trans: I speak in my own words.

meanings.note: The most dramatic or impressive moment in a performance or story.

examples.text: いよいよ映画の見せ場だ。
examples.trans: At last, it's the highlight of the movie.

examples.text: ここが彼の見せ場です。
examples.trans: This is his moment to shine.

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: この映画はとても面白いです。
何か面白い話はありませんか。
examples.trans: Do you have any interesting stories?
